newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania puts NATO admission costs at $3 bln.
newsitem.headline: Romania puts NATO admission costs at $3 bln.

text.p: Romania's Defence Minister on Thursday put a price tag of $3 billion on the cost of the country's quick integration into NATO and said the United States had no reason to oppose its bid for early entry.

"Expansion costs are a heavy argument for the United States' decision. Now we can also show what the specific cost of expansion is for Romania -- around $3 billion over the next eight years," Victor Babiuc told a news conference.

"Romania meets all the admission criteria and there are no significant differences betwen us and the favourites. We expect to be invited to join. It would consolidate the alliance, especially its southern flank."
Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is spending a week in Washington to try to persuade U.S. officials to reverse their decision to oppose early Romanian membership.
The United States last week said it favoured including only Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic when the Alliance announces its first expansion at a July 8-9 summit in Madrid.
That left out Romania and Slovenia but U.S. officials said both had made good progress and were prime candidates for subsequent enlargement.
Ciorbea, who met Vice President Al Gore on Wednesday, said Romania would "fight to the very end" to gain first-group membership. He is due to meet U.S. Secretary of Defence William Cohen on Friday.
Romania, whose army ranks second in size only to Poland's among the 12 candidates for NATO membership, says it can shoulder its own integration bill.
A senior defence ministry official said last week Romania would go ahead with a $1.5 billion deal to buy NATO-compatible helicopters, whether it gained first-wave entry to NATO or not.

The defence ministry said it would buy 96 AH-1RO Dracula helicopters to be co-produced by a venture between Romania's Intreprinderea Aeronautica Romana (IAR) aircraft maker and U.S. firm Bell Helicopter Textron.
